script: Spread and total were not saved, so this script is inferred only from three-game form. ARI has been a J.Love run game (41 carries, 160 yards) with targets piled on T.McBride (34 targets, 211 yards) and Mi.Wilson (31 targets, 163 yards), while NYG has handed C.Skattebo 50 carries for 177 yards and thrown most often to I.Likely (23 targets, 124 yards). Both defenses have leaked on the ground (NYG 4.94 YPC, ARI 4.63 YPC), so with no number there is no basis to call a shootout or a grind — the bell-cows stay involved and the target hierarchies hold.
who_goes_off: T.McBride is the ARI player who should go off: 70.3 receiving yards per game on 34 targets, into the only NYG pass location above 7.0 YPA, the middle at 8.11 on 9 attempts, while the perimeter sits at 6.72 left and 6.69 right. For NYG, I.Likely is the one already converting (124 yards on 23 targets, 133 air yards) and D.Mooney has cashed his air (95 receiving yards on 91 air yards, 8 targets) against an ARI defense that allowed 9 passes of 20+ on 84 attempts; M.Nabers has 185 air yards but only 96 yards on 19 targets, so recent form does not say he goes off.
weak_spot: NYG's real weak spot is the run — 4.94 yards per carry and 9 runs of 10+ — and the middle at 8.11 YPA, not the outside, where they have allowed 6.72 YPA on 46 left attempts, 6.69 on 45 right attempts, and only 6 passes of 20+ on 101 attempts. ARI's weak spot is coverage on every side: 9.58 YPA left (26 attempts), 9.20 middle (25 attempts), 9.03 right (29 attempts), plus 9 explosives on 84 attempts and a run defense at 4.63 YPC with 11 runs of 10+.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for ARI@NYG, so there is no injury fallout to price. The role split in the three-game log is the fallout that matters: J.Love 41 carries to T.Allgeier's 24 and J.Brissett's 8, C.Skattebo 50 carries to N.Harris's 13 and D.Singletary's 9, T.McBride and Mi.Wilson at 34 and 31 targets against M.Harrison's 9, and I.Likely at 23 targets against T.Johnson's 5.
qb_vs_blitz: ARI's QB is -0.12 EPA per dropback versus the blitz (n=28) and +0.18 with no blitz, and NYG blitzes only 26%, so most ARI dropbacks project into the +0.18 split that keeps T.McBride's 34-target role live. NYG's QB is -0.62 versus the blitz (n=29) and +0.28 with no blitz, and ARI blitzes only 22%, so NYG dropbacks project into the +0.28 environment even though M.Nabers (96 yards on 185 air yards) and M.Fields (74 yards on 213 air yards) have not matched the air yards.

picks.why: K.Bourne has 14 targets and 108 receiving yards over these three games (36.0 per game) on only 56 air yards, a short YAC profile that does not need the explosives NYG has limited to 6 on 101 attempts. The 20.5 line is 15.5 yards under that rate, and even a clamp toward NYG's 6.69-6.72 outside YPA still clears 20.5 on about 4 targets, while the board prices him under M.Harrison's 34.5 despite Bourne's 108 yards to Harrison's 73.

M.Harrison has 9 targets and 73 yards (24.3 per game) with 159 air yards, a low-volume shot profile into the NYG perimeter that has allowed 6.72 YPA left, 6.69 right, and 6 passes of 20+ on 101 attempts. Clearing 34.5 needs about 11.5 yards per target on a 3-target rate, above the 8.1 yards per target on those 9 targets, while T.McBride (34 targets, 211 yards) and Mi.Wilson (31 targets, 163 yards) keep the ARI target share.
